metadata.title: Ellipsoid fitting and GaussianAnalysis: source catalogue
notes: The original bundle contains three mathematical results. The 37 checked reports are not a count of all mathematical theorems or all library lemmas.
Application targets are T1–T7 and T9–T14; there is no T8.
Source paths, declaration names and line anchors were validated locally against source_commit. Live GitHub responses were not checked.
Every entry links a proved theorem; statement-only files are secondary links.
The existing doc/libdoc/site is a historical phase12 rendering at 904688306c080bccbf2acc617c523a59cfc6899b and is not the current catalogue.

entries.title: Three Gaussian ellipsoid-fitting results
entries.summary: The probability of a positive semidefinite fit tends to one below density 1/4 and to zero above it. Below the threshold, fits can also have trace d and fixed positive spectral bounds. Balanced positive-definite combinations of sample outer products have the opposite transition.
assumptions: Independent standard Gaussian points in dimension d; sample sizes n(d).
The fitting transition uses limsup n/d² < 1/4 or liminf n/d² > 1/4.
For every alpha < 1/4, the well-conditioned result assumes limsup n/d² ≤ alpha; its spectral constants depend only on alpha.
notes: One formal theorem bundles three mathematical results and includes measurability of their events.
No claim at the critical density follows from these threshold statements.
Formalization of the three main results of Misiakiewicz and Wen.

entries.title: Universality and finite or countable mixtures
entries.summary: A sharp fitting transition at alpha_*(kappa), bounded-condition positive definite fits below it, and a deterministic limiting fitting error extend from independent coordinates to finite and countable mixtures of product laws.
assumptions: Samples are independent and identically distributed; n/d² tends to alpha > 0.
Within each mixture component, coordinates are independent, mean zero, variance one, and uniformly subgaussian with one constant K > 0.
Every coordinate has unconditional fourth moment kappa > 1 after averaging over the mixture.
Mixture families and their weights may depend on dimension.
notes: Coordinates of a point may be dependent under the mixture.
A component need not itself have fourth moment kappa.
The independent-coordinate result formalizes Koehler and Sohn; the mixture extension is stated separately.

entries.title: The optimal condition number
entries.summary: For every C > 1, the probability of an exact fit with condition number at most C has threshold alpha(C,kappa). Below alpha_*(kappa), the optimal condition number converges in probability to C_*(alpha,kappa), the inverse curve.
assumptions: Admissible finite or countable mixtures of product laws, with common subgaussian bound K > 0 and unconditional fourth moment kappa > 1.
n/d² tends to alpha > 0; convergence of the optimum assumes 0 < alpha < alpha_*(kappa).
notes: Nothing is asserted at alpha = alpha(C,kappa).
The condition number is the matrix eigenvalue ratio; the ellipsoid semiaxis ratio is its square root.
At kappa = 3, alpha_*(3) = 1/4.

entries.title: Robustness to small changes of law
entries.summary: The condition-number threshold and limiting optimum persist when the point law is within o(d⁻²) in total variation of an admissible finite or countable mixture.
assumptions: Reference families satisfy the mixture assumptions with kappa > 1 and K > 0.
d² times the total-variation discrepancy tends to zero.
The threshold comparison is away from alpha(C,kappa); the optimum limit is below alpha_*(kappa).
notes: A separate contamination example shows that O(d⁻²) cannot replace o(d⁻²) in general.

entries.title: Explicit dependent point laws
entries.summary: Paired coordinates and a single latent sign shared across all coordinates yield explicit dependent laws with sharp fitting transitions. The latent-sign theorem also gives the limiting fitting error and small-residual interpolation.
assumptions: Paired-law parameter −1 ≤ eps ≤ 7/3.
Latent-sign parameter 0 ≤ s ≤ 1, allowed to depend on dimension; the unconditional coordinate fourth moment is 9/5.
Independent samples with n/d² tending to a positive density.
notes: The condition and interpolation constants in the latent-sign result are uniform over s in [0,1].

entries.title: Dependence and the limits of the mixture model
entries.summary: For the latent-sign law, variance-tensorization constants can grow exponentially with dimension, despite exact fitting below the threshold. A continuous latent mixture can remain at total-variation distance one from every countable mixture of product laws.
assumptions: The exponential lower-bound result concerns a fixed latent-sign parameter s > 0 in the specified latent-sign family.
The matching upper-bound theorem covers 0 ≤ s ≤ 1.
The continuous-mixture result concerns its explicitly constructed law; it is not a claim about every continuous mixture.
notes: The upper tensorization bound is 2 ((1+s)/(1−3s/7))^d.

entries.title: S1 · Small Gaussian shifts preserve the optimum
entries.summary: The centered-Gaussian condition-number threshold and limiting optimum are unchanged by deterministic shifts small compared with sqrt(d).
assumptions: Independent N(m_d,I_d) points; n/d² → alpha > 0.
||m_d||/sqrt(d) → 0; C > 1 for the threshold.
The optimal-condition limit assumes 0 < alpha < 1/4.
notes: Equality at the condition-number threshold is left open.

entries.title: S2 · Arbitrary Gaussian shifts: the cost of translation
entries.summary: Below density 1/4, positive definite fits exist and the optimal condition number is of order 1 + ||m_d||/sqrt(d). A lower bound on that scale holds uniformly over translations at every positive density.
assumptions: Independent standard Gaussian samples translated by a deterministic sequence m_d.
n/d² → alpha > 0; the existence and two-sided bounds require alpha < 1/4.
No bound is imposed on the shift magnitudes.
notes: The lower bound holds on one high-probability event for all translations. The upper/existence statement applies to each deterministic shift sequence.

entries.title: S3 · Above the Gaussian threshold: no PSD quadric
entries.summary: One high-probability event excludes every quadric whose quadratic part is positive semidefinite and nonzero, whatever its linear and constant terms. It therefore excludes a centered fit after every translation.
assumptions: Independent standard Gaussian points; n/d² → alpha > 1/4.
notes: The event is chosen before the quadric; this is simultaneous over all such quadrics.

entries.title: S4 · Fitting error is unchanged by Gaussian shifts
entries.summary: At every positive density, arbitrary deterministic shifts preserve the limiting fitting error e_*(alpha,3). Taking the infimum over all translations has the same limit.
assumptions: Independent standard Gaussian samples; n/d² → alpha > 0.
Arbitrary deterministic shift sequences.
notes: The density alpha = 1/4 is included for the error limit. A zero limiting error does not prove exact fitting at that density.

entries.title: S5 · Symmetric mixtures exclude all PSD quadrics
entries.summary: Above alpha_*(kappa), symmetric mixture point laws have a positive fitting-error margin uniform over translations, and no quadric with nonzero positive semidefinite quadratic part fits all points.
assumptions: Finite or countable admissible mixtures; kappa > 1 and a uniform subgaussian bound K > 0.
The point law is centrally symmetric; individual mixture components need not be.
n/d² → alpha > alpha_*(kappa).
notes: The positive margin is chosen from kappa and alpha before K and the family.
The theorem supplies measurable good events; it does not assert measurability of the existential arbitrary-quadric event.

entries.title: S6 · Sparse shifts preserve mixture fitting
entries.summary: Below alpha_*(kappa), deterministic shifts supported on o(d) coordinates preserve positive definite fits with probability tending to one.
assumptions: Finite or countable admissible mixtures; kappa > 1, K > 0, and n/d² → alpha in (0,alpha_*(kappa)).
The number of nonzero shift coordinates divided by d tends to zero.
notes: No symmetry and no bound on shift magnitudes are required. The support may change with dimension.
The assertion is for each shift sequence, not one event simultaneously covering all shifts.

entries.title: S7 · Opposite shifts have the same fitting statistics
entries.summary: For a centrally symmetric point law, a mixture of its translates by m and −m has exactly the same joint outer-product law as the translate by m. Centered-fit probabilities, optimal condition numbers and fitting errors therefore agree.
assumptions: Independent samples from a centrally symmetric point law.
Any mixture weight in [0,1], including endpoints.
The stated Gaussian and admissible-mixture asymptotic consequences use the hypotheses of S1, S2, S5 or S6 as applicable.
notes: This does not transfer arbitrary-center quadric events or an infimum over additional translations.

entries.title: T1 · Gaussian matrix series
entries.summary: Even trace-moment bounds for symmetric Gaussian matrix series, operator-norm bounds for rectangular series, and a quantitative bound under variance and trace control.
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; fixed real matrices and independent standard Gaussian coefficients.
Symmetry is required for the trace-moment clause; moment order q is positive.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.

entries.title: T2 · Tensor packing
entries.summary: Bounds how many tensor pairs can have large projection onto a low-dimensional matrix subspace, given controlled correlations.
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; vector families in Euclidean unit balls.
Correlation graphs have degree at most L; correlations outside them are at most eta ≤ eps²/10000.
0 < eps ≤ 1; an orthonormal matrix family has size at most d, with d > 0.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.

entries.title: T3 · The upper spectral edge of the GOE
entries.summary: The normalized GOE has expected largest eigenvalue at most 2 and Gaussian upper tails; analogous bounds control the negative edge and operator norm.
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; the normalized Gaussian orthogonal ensemble in dimension d ≥ 1.
Tail parameter t ≥ 0.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.

entries.title: T4 · The high-temperature SK spectral gap
entries.summary: With high probability over the Gaussian disorder, the SK heat-bath spectral gap is at least (1−2 beta)/2, with a corresponding covariance bound, uniformly over external fields and interaction scalings.
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; 0 ≤ beta < 1/2.
Interaction scaling s in [0,1]; arbitrary external fields.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.

entries.title: T5 · Orthogonal splitting of PSD matrices
entries.summary: Splits the identity into orthogonal projections and controls the cross-energy of a finite PSD matrix family by its pairwise trace overlaps.
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; a nonempty finite family of positive semidefinite square matrices.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.

entries.title: T6 · Sign/Gaussian comparison for the perceptron
entries.summary: The expected Ising-perceptron pressures for sign and Gaussian patterns differ by at most C M N^(−3/2).
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; N > 0 variables and M patterns.
The test function and its first three derivatives satisfy the stated uniform bounds; C depends on those bounds.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.

entries.title: T7 · Concentration of random SAT lifetime
entries.summary: The variance of the capped largest satisfiable prefix of independent uniform proper signed k-clauses is O_k(n^(1+2/k)).
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; fixed k ≥ 3 and n ≥ k+1.
The prefix length is capped at 2^(k+1)n.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.

entries.title: T9 · A limiting threshold for every fixed k-SAT
entries.summary: For every fixed k ≥ 3, a positive limiting density separates asymptotically satisfiable and unsatisfiable random k-SAT instances.
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; independent uniform proper signed k-clauses on n variables.
The clause count is floor(c n), for a fixed density c on either side of the threshold.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.
The theorem establishes existence of the limiting threshold, not an explicit formula for its value; equality is not asserted.

entries.title: T10 · Exact normalization of PSD factors
entries.summary: Preserves every trace pairing and factor size while bounding the traces of one factor family by m and the other by the factor dimension r.
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; finite PSD matrix families F_i and G_j of size r, with the second index set nonempty.
Every trace pairing tr(F_i G_j) is at most m.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.

entries.title: T11 · Product smoothing of matrix squares
entries.summary: A product-averaged PSD matrix-valued function admits a sum-of-squares representation with quantitative weighted Fourier-coefficient bounds.
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; finite product spaces and the stated smoothing_hyps.
The matrix-valued function is positive semidefinite with trace at most B.
The positive weight lambda and smoothing parameters satisfy the explicit smallness inequality in the statement.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.

entries.title: T12 · Convergence from approximate minimum inequalities
entries.summary: Bounded sequences satisfying balanced approximate minimum inequalities and a neighboring-term lower bound converge, with an explicit lower estimate for the limit.
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; nonnegative error constant A and exponent beta > 0.
Beyond a fixed index, the two lower inequalities hold with error A min(r,s)^(−beta) or A s^(−beta).
Boundedness is needed for convergence; the finite-index lower estimate is also proved without it.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.

entries.title: T13 · Exponential PSD rank of shifted matching matrices
entries.summary: There is a positive integer K, uniform in 0 < rho < 1, such that every size-r PSD factorization of A_n(rho) satisfies 2^n ≤ r^K for sufficiently large even n.
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; 0 < rho < 1; even n beyond a threshold that may depend on rho.
A_n(rho) has entries |M ∩ delta(U)| − 1 + rho, indexed by odd vertex sets and perfect matchings.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.
Quantifier order: for every realType R, there is K > 0; for every rho in (0,1), there is n0. Do not claim n0 is uniform in rho.
The source header distinguishes this exponential conclusion from the different superpolynomial Lean statement in the collection.

entries.title: T14 · Exponential lower bounds for exact PSD lifts
entries.summary: The unshifted matching matrix, its full slack matrix and exact semidefinite lifts of the perfect matching polytope all satisfy exponential size lower bounds.
assumptions: An arbitrary realType; all sufficiently large even n.
A PSD factorization of A_n(0) or T_n(0), or an exact semidefinite lift of the perfect matching polytope.
notes: Formalization of a credited argument from the OpenAI math collection, revision 1581d4cbd; the source header records the precise correspondence.
The source header distinguishes this exponential conclusion from the different superpolynomial Lean statement in the collection.

entries.title: Gaussian measures and integration
entries.summary: Gaussian measures on vectors and matrices, moments, Gaussian integration by parts, parameter integrals and covariance interpolation.
assumptions: The representative integration-by-parts result is over an arbitrary realType.
The function and its continuous coordinate derivative satisfy the stated polynomial-growth bounds.
notes: The linked theorem is one representative result; its assumptions do not describe every result in this directory.
GaussianAnalysis is written over arbitrary MathComp real structures. This catalog does not assert that every library statement has received human review.

entries.title: Gaussian comparison and concentration
entries.summary: Gaussian concentration and Poincare inequalities; Slepian, Sudakov–Fernique, Gordon, CGMT and Brascamp–Lieb inequalities.
assumptions: The representative Sudakov–Fernique theorem compares finite centered Gaussian linear processes.
Every increment variance of the first process is at most the corresponding increment variance of the second.
notes: The linked theorem is one representative result; its assumptions do not describe every result in this directory.

entries.title: Matrix geometry and PSD factorizations
entries.summary: Spectral decompositions, matrix norms, projections, effective rank, PSD factorizations, spectral multiplicity and centered matrix corrections.
assumptions: The representative trace-penalized maximization result assumes a nonempty closed convex set of real matrices and penalty parameter c > −1.
notes: The linked theorem is one representative result; its assumptions do not describe every result in this directory.

entries.title: Probability and replacement arguments
entries.summary: Product laws, Lindeberg replacement, Efron–Stein and Hanson–Wright inequalities, subgaussian and subexponential bounds, mixtures and symmetric row laws.
assumptions: The representative Efron–Stein result concerns independent coordinates under a finite product law and a square-integrable function.
notes: The linked theorem is one representative result; its assumptions do not describe every result in this directory.

entries.title: Fourier analysis and small-ball estimates
entries.summary: Characteristic functions, Fourier inversion, concentration functions, vector small-ball bounds and Fourier analysis on Boolean products.
assumptions: The representative vector small-ball estimate assumes independent scalar variables with uniformly bounded second moments and a uniform anticoncentration bound.
Coefficient vectors satisfy a lower-frame bound and a maximum-norm bound; the ball scale is above the stated multiple of that maximum norm.
notes: The linked theorem is one representative result; its assumptions do not describe every result in this directory.

entries.title: Convex geometry and optimization
entries.summary: Self-concordant barriers, regularized minimizers, Moreau decomposition, image projections and residual directions of PSD trace slices.
assumptions: The representative Moreau theorem assumes a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional real space.
notes: The linked theorem is one representative result; its assumptions do not describe every result in this directory.

entries.title: Random matrices and reserve corrections
entries.summary: GOE spectral estimates, restricted isometry, Gaussian and Rademacher matrix series, isotropic rows, row-sign invariance and reserve corrections.
assumptions: The representative matrix-series theorem uses fixed symmetric real matrices of size n ≥ 1 and independent uniform signs.
Its expected operator-norm bound is 40 sqrt(log(2n)) sqrt(||sum A_j²||).
notes: The linked theorem is one representative result; its assumptions do not describe every result in this directory.

entries.title: Analysis of limits and measurable infima
entries.summary: Convergence from approximate minimum inequalities, measurable infima of continuous functions and transfer along cofinal dimension maps.
assumptions: The representative transfer theorem assumes a property eventually valid for every admissible full family with the specified limiting statistic.
An admissible baseline with that statistic limit exists; the new dimension map is cofinal and the reindexed family has the same limit.
notes: The linked theorem is one representative result; its assumptions do not describe every result in this directory.

entries.title: Finite combinatorics
entries.summary: Binomial coefficient estimates, finite permutation expanders and the harmonic-number bound H_n ≤ 1 + ln n.
assumptions: The representative expander existence theorem assumes a positive natural size l.
One hundred permutations yield the stated bipartite multigraph cut-expansion property.
notes: The linked theorem is one representative result; its assumptions do not describe every result in this directory.
